title: Spotting Fake Internships & Digital Arrest Scams
objectives: Identify red flags in internship/job offers that require registration fees
Understand the importance of independent verification before sharing personal info
Know how to report suspected cybercrime through official channels

stages.task: Gather credible sources on fake internship scams and digital arrest intimidation, ensuring no fabricated statistics or contact details are used.
Draft a clear, practical, calm narrative that warns about suspicious registration fees, digital arrest intimidation, independent verification, and official reporting guidance.
Create visual sequences that illustrate red flag signs, verification steps, and safe reporting actions without using fear-based imagery or implying fictional examples are real cases.
Produce graphics and animations that depict warning signs, verification tools, and official reporting channels, avoiding any fabricated data.
Assemble the video ensuring pacing fits 48 seconds, tone remains calm, and all content aligns with the objectives and must_include points.

Review the final reel for compliance with safety guidelines, ensuring no victim-blaming, no fabricated statistics, and that the CTA clearly states to verify independently and report through official channels.

safety_checks: Verify legitimacy of any job/internship offer through official company channels or reputable job boards
Do not share OTPs, passwords, or other credentials in response to unsolicited requests
Report suspicious offers or intimidation messages to campus IT or local law enforcement via official reporting channels
Ensure all content is factual and does not present fictional scenarios as real cases
